verdict.rationale: GitLab documents self-hosted installation through a Linux package, official Docker images, self-compilation for unsupported distributions, and Helm/Operator for Kubernetes, so the core self-hosting part of the story is delivered. Nothing in the pack shows low-resource operation, support for multiple CPU architectures, or a choice of database backends. Distribution coverage is only implied, and Docker and Kubernetes support are host-platform capabilities rather than broad OS support by GitLab itself. Missing for 10: evidence of low-resource or minimal-footprint operation, documented multi-CPU-architecture support, support for multiple database backends, explicit multi-OS support beyond Linux, and hands-on corroboration on constrained hardware.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can run a self-hosted instance on low-resource hardware across multiple OSes, CPU architectures, and database backends

citations.quote: The Linux package includes services and tools to install GitLab without laborious configuration.
If the Linux package isn't available for your distribution, you can self-compile GitLab.
GitLab maintains a set of official Docker images based on the Linux package.
One user has long run GitLab in a VM using the TurnKey Linux appliance.
